audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer gives Ryze two roots and makes them unconditional. spikes[0] 'his Q-into-E root poke and W root', early 'Ryze's Q-into-E combo roots you and his W is a second hard root', wants.foe[0] 'Land Q-into-E to root you, then chain W root', whys[0] 'his Q-into-E root plus W root'.
audit.why: Ryze has exactly one root and it is conditional. Rune Prison (W): 'Ryze traps a target in a cage of runes, damaging them and slowing their movement. If the target has Flux on it, they are instead rooted.' Overload (Q) and Spell Flux (E) apply no root at all — E applies the Flux debuff, which is the enabler. This matters enormously for Nasus specifically: a root stops him walking at you, a slow does not. A player who believes he is facing a two-root chain will refuse windows where Rune Prison would only have slowed him, and will never learn to watch for the Flux debuff — which is the actual read.
audit.corrected: Rune Prison is Ryze's only root, and only when Spell Flux is already on you. Without Flux it is a slow you can keep walking through.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ryze.json (Q Overload, W Rune Prison, E Spell Flux)

audit.whatIsWrong: The range gap between Wither and Ryze's root combo is never stated, in a lane entirely decided by it.
audit.why: Wither is 700 range. Rune Prison and Spell Flux are both 615. Nasus can land his slow from 85 units outside the range of either half of Ryze's root setup — that is the whole reason the level-6 window works, and it is nowhere in either layer. Overload at 1000 is the only thing that reaches him, and it is a line shot the front minion eats ('dealing damage to the first enemy struck').
audit.corrected: Wither reaches 700; Rune Prison and Spell Flux both stop at 615. Slow him from outside his root range.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] and whys[6] attribute Overload's cooldown resets to rooting — 'his rooted Q resets', 'rooted spell rotations'.
audit.why: Overload's passive is 'Ryze's other basic abilities reset the cooldown of Overload and charge a rune.' The resets come from casting W or E, with no root involved. Framing the resets as root-dependent teaches the wrong tell — a player will assume that avoiding the root avoids the DPS, when Ryze's rotation resets regardless.
audit.corrected: Every Rune Prison or Spell Flux cast resets Overload — the rotation runs whether or not you are rooted.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0] call Rune Prison a 'point-blank root'.
audit.why: It is 615 range, which is not point-blank — it is longer than most melee engage tools and, critically, only 85 units shorter than Wither. Describing it as point-blank encourages a player to think stepping just outside melee range is safe, when it is not.
audit.corrected: Rune Prison is 615 range on an 11s cooldown at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: content 'late' and whys[6] describe Realm Warp as map pressure a splitpush cannot out-tempo.
audit.why: Realm Warp is 3000 range on a 180/160/140 cooldown and carries no global flag in the kit — contrast Shen's Stand United at 35000 with an explicit global flag. It repositions a group a screen and a half, it does not answer a splitpush from across the map. Overstating it tells a Nasus his splitpush is dead when it is in fact his best remaining path.
audit.corrected: Realm Warp is 3000 range on a 180s cooldown at rank 1 — it collapses on your side lane only if his team is already close.
sources: champ-data/_kits/shen.json (R Stand United — global flag, for contrast)

notes: The packet's suspectNames for this matchup are BOTH false positives and should not be acted on: wants.you[2] 'Use Spirit Fire' and whys[0] 'No Wither' are Nasus's own E and W, spelled correctly. The near-miss detector is matching owner abilities against the enemy's ability list. Worth a filter fix, because the same pattern will fire on every Nasus, Cassiopeia and Brand entry that correctly names its own kit. The real error in this matchup was the opposite of what the detector flagged: the ability names present were fine, but the mechanics attached to them were invented — Ryze was given two unconditional roots when he has one conditional one. Also note the 'root chain' phrasing appears across several fields here and reads templated; other owners' Ryze entries are worth grepping for 'Q-into-E root' and 'W root'.
